articles.title: A ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city holds for its first 30 hours, officials say
articles.description: A six-day ceasefire has been initiated in Oleshky, allowing much-needed humanitarian aid for around 2,000 residents. Both Ukraine and Russia have reported no violations of the ceasefire in the first 30 hours. Negotiations continue for future discussions to de-escalate the ongoing war, despite both sides holding firm on key demands. Meanwhile, attacks have intensified elsewhere, including drone strikes causing injuries in cities like Kharkiv.

articles.title: A ceasefire in a Ukrainian city is holding, officials say, as Moscow and Kyiv await US-led talks
articles.description: Officials say that a six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in southern Ukraine has held for its first day and night. The truce began Tuesday and aims to provide food, medicine and evacuation for about 2,000 residents. It will be the first significant truce since Russia’s full-scale invasion began nearly five years ago. That's if it's successful. U.S. first lady Melania Trump brokered the humanitarian mission and Pope Leo XIV urged the provision of aid and safe evacuations. The war rages on elsewhere with Russian drone strikes in Kharkiv and Ukrainian drones downed in Russia.

articles.title: US and Russia discuss Sakhalin venture and Druzhba pipeline revival
articles.description: The US and Russia are discussing a joint oil venture off the Sakhalin coast as part of broader Ukraine peace negotiations, per the Financial Times. The two sides are also discussing incorporating US majors in a plan to resume Russian oil deliveries to Europe through the Druzhba pipeline. Both potential accords are part of a larger US effort to terminate the invasion by offering incentives. US leaders have said the ventures would not begin until the conflict was done.

articles.title: Melania Trump Announces Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire Near Oleshky, Says Humanitarian Access Expanded
articles.description: US First Lady Melania Trump announced that a localised Russia-Ukraine ceasefire took effect on October 27, two days early, and expanded beyond Oleshky in the Kherson region. She said the arrangement would allow humanitarian aid deliveries and civilian evacuations. The White House said both countries helped coordinate the plan, but the report does not independently verify its implementation.
